nodes.name: Theorem 2.1: Concentration of sample moment tensors
nodes.statement:
Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered sub-Gaussian random
vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and
sub-Gaussian constant \(K\). Let \(p\ge 2\) be an integer. Then, for every
\(q\ge1\),
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(
\mathbb{E}
\bigg\|
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}
-
\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}
\bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}
\lesssim_p
K^p
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N}
+
\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}
+
\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right),
\]
where
\[
\rho_p(\Sigma)
:=
\begin{cases}
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2},
& p \text{ even},\\[3pt]
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2},
& p \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]
Moreover, if $X$ is Gaussian, then
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E} \bigg\|
\frac{1}{N}
\sum_{i=1}^N
X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}
\bigg\|_{\mathsf{F}}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}
\asymp_p
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt{N}}
+
\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q}{N}}
+
\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N},
\]
where
\[
\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)
:=
\begin{cases}
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt]
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1: Square-function weak-moment reduction
nodes.statement:
Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\) be independent centered random vectors in a real
Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), let \(q\ge2\), and assume that
\[
\|Z_i\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)}
:=
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(
\mathbb{E}\|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^q
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}
<\infty,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,N.
\]
Then
\[
\bigg\|
\sum_{i=1}^N Z_i
\bigg\|_{L_q(\mathcal H)}
\asymp
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\|
\bigg(
\sum_{i=1}^N \|Z_i\|_{\mathcal H}^2
\bigg)^{1/2}
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_q}
+
\sup_{\|h\|_{\mathcal H}=1}
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\|
\sum_{i=1}^N
\langle h,Z_i\rangle_{\mathcal H}
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{L_{q/2}}.
\]

Lemma 3.5: Weak tensor moments
Proposition 2.4: Moment tensors of uniformly log-concave distributions
nodes.statement:
Let \(\Sigma\) be positive definite, and let \(Y\in\mathbb R^d\) be a
centered random vector with density \(c\exp(-V(y))\), where \(c>0\) is
the normalizing constant and \(V\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)\) satisfies
\(\nabla^2V(y)\succeq\Sigma^{-1}\) for every \(y\in\mathbb R^d\).
Then, for every integer \(p\ge2\),
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\|
\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p}
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\|_{\mathsf F}
\lesssim_p
\rho_p(\Sigma),  \qquad
\rho_p(\Sigma)
:=
\begin{cases}
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2},
& p \text{ even},\\[3pt]
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2},
& p \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]

nodes.name: Theorem 2.2: Polynomial moments under Gaussian convex domination
nodes.statement:
Let \(G_\Sigma\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)\), where
\(\Sigma\succeq0\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^d\) be a centered random
vector such that \(Z\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}G_\Sigma\). Then, for every
integer \(p\ge1\), every \(q\ge1\), every finite-dimensional Hilbert
space \(\mathcal H\), and every \(p\)-linear map
\[
T:(\mathbb R^d)^p\to\mathcal H,
\]
one has
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(
\mathbb{E}
\big\|
T(Z,\ldots,Z)
\big\|_{\mathcal H}^q
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}
\lesssim_p
\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|T\|_{\mathsf F}.
\]

nodes.name: Proposition 2.3: Polynomial moments for Gaussian vectors
nodes.statement:
Let \(G_\Sigma\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)\), where
\(\Sigma\succeq0\). Then, for every integer \(p\ge1\), every \(q\ge1\),
every finite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and every
\(p\)-linear map
\[
T:(\mathbb R^d)^p\to\mathcal H,
\]
one has
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(
\mathbb{E}
\big\|
T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)
\big\|_{\mathcal H}^q
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}
\lesssim_p
\Psi_p(q,\Sigma)\|T\|_{\mathsf F},
\]
and
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(
\mathbb{E}
\big\|
T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)
-
\mathbb{E} T(G_\Sigma,\ldots,G_\Sigma)
\big\|_{\mathcal H}^q
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}
\lesssim_p
\Psi_p^\circ(q,\Sigma)\|T\|_{\mathsf F},
\]
where $\Psi_{p}(q,\Sigma)$ and $\Psi_p^\circ(q,\Sigma)$ are defined in (2.5).

nodes.name: Theorem 2.1: Example Sharpness of
nodes.statement:
Fix an integer \(p\ge2\). Let
\[
\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_d>0,
\qquad
\Lambda:=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d),
\qquad
\lambda_1=\|\Lambda\|.
\]
Let \(G\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Lambda)\), let
\(\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}^d\) have independent Rademacher entries, and let
\(R\), independent of \(G\) and \(\varepsilon\), take the values \(0\) and
\(\sqrt2\), each with probability \(1/2\). Define
\[
Y:=R\Lambda^{1/2}\varepsilon,
\qquad
X:=(G,Y)\in\mathbb R^{2d}.
\]
Standard Gaussian and Rademacher sub-Gaussian estimates, together with the
boundedness of \(R\), show that \(X\) satisfies (2.1) with
\(K\asymp1\). Since \(\mathbb{E} R^2=1\), \(X\) is centered and has covariance matrix
\[
\Sigma
=
\begin{bmatrix}
\Lambda&0\\
0&\Lambda
\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)=2\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda),
\qquad
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}=\sqrt2 \|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F},
\qquad
\|\Sigma\|=\|\Lambda\|.
\end{equation}


For \(i=1,\ldots,N\), let \((G_i,R_i,\varepsilon_i)\) be independent
copies of \((G,R,\varepsilon)\), and set
\[
Y_i:=R_i\Lambda^{1/2}\varepsilon_i,
\qquad
X_i:=(G_i,Y_i).
\]
Then \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are i.i.d. with the same distribution as \(X\). Let
\[
S_p
:=
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} X^{\otimes p}.
\]
We show that, for every \(q\ge1\),
\begin{equation}
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}
\gtrsim_p
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N}
+
\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}
+
\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N},
\end{equation}
where \(\rho_p(\Sigma)\) is defined in Theorem 2.1.

Restricting \(S_p\) to the tensor block corresponding entirely to the
\(G\)-coordinates, we obtain
\[
\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}
\ge
\bigg\|
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N G_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} G^{\otimes p}
\bigg\|_{\mathsf F}.
\]
The Gaussian lower bound in Theorem~2.1 therefore yields
\begin{equation}
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}
\gtrsim_p
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N}
+
\rho_{p,G}(\Lambda)\sqrt{\frac qN}
+
\|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}.
\end{equation}

Suppose first that \(p\) is odd. In this case,
\[
\rho_{p,G}(\Lambda)
=
\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Lambda\|^{1/2}
=
\rho_p(\Lambda).
\]
Moreover, $\sqrt{\frac qN}
\ge
\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}$.
Thus (3.20) follows from
(3.21) and
(3.19).

Now suppose that \(p=2k\) is even. Retaining the first and third terms in
(3.21), we have
\begin{equation}
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}
\gtrsim_p
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Lambda)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N}
+
\|\Lambda\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}.
\end{equation}
It remains to obtain the intermediate fluctuation scale lower bound. Set
\[
B:=\frac{\Lambda}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}},
\qquad
A:=B^{\otimes k}.
\]
Then
\[
\|A\|_{\mathsf F}
=
\|B\|_{\mathsf F}^k
=
1.
\]
Since $\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p}$
is the tensor block of \(S_p\) corresponding entirely to the
\(Y\)-coordinates, we have
\begin{equation}
\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}
\ge
\bigg\|
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p}
\bigg\|_{\mathsf F}
\ge
\bigg|
\bigg\langle
A,
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p}
\bigg\rangle_{\mathsf F}
\bigg|.
\end{equation}

Since \(Y=R\Lambda^{1/2}\varepsilon\) and every coordinate of \(\varepsilon\) takes values in \(\{\pm 1\}\),
\[
Y^\top B Y
=
\frac{R^2}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}}
\varepsilon^\top\Lambda^2\varepsilon
=
\frac{R^2}{\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}}
\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j^2
=
R^2\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}.
\]
Consequently, recalling that \(p=2k\),
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle A,Y^{\otimes p}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F}
=
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left\langle B^{\otimes k},Y^{\otimes 2k}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right\rangle_{\mathsf F}
=
(Y^\top B Y)^k
=
R^{2k}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k.
\]
For \( i = 1, \ldots, N\), define the Rademacher random variable \(\eta_i\) by 
\[
R_i^{2k}-\mathbb{E} R^{2k}
=
2^{k-1}\eta_i.
\]
Then \(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_N\) are independent, and
\[
\bigg\langle
A,
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbb{E} Y^{\otimes p}
\bigg\rangle_{\mathsf F}
=
2^{k-1}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\eta_i.
\]
Combining this identity with
(3.23) and taking \(L_q\)-norms, we obtain
\begin{align}
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{E}\|S_p\|_{\mathsf F}^q\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{1/q}
\ge
2^{k-1}\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^k
\bigg\|
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\eta_i
\bigg\|_{L_q}
\asymp_p
\|\Lambda\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2}
\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}},

\end{align}
where the last step follows from the two-sided moment estimate for
Rademacher sums
[montgomerysmith1990rademacher].
Combining (3.22) and
(3.24), and using
(3.19), proves
(3.20) in the even case.
